findings.title: CISA, FBI, HHS, USDA, and DOT Urge Critical Infrastructure To Strengthen Industrial Refrigeration and Cold Chain Monitoring Systems Cybersecurity
findings.summary_md: CISA, the FBI, HHS, USDA and DOT published a joint fact sheet warning that malicious actors are targeting unpatched or internet-accessible electronic temperature controllers and commercial refrigeration controllers in grocery and cold storage facilities. The agencies said successful exploitation could let actors change temperatures and cause fire hazards, inventory loss and changes to system service life. The release identifies healthcare, chemical, food and agriculture, and transportation as sectors where these systems are widely used.

findings.title: The fridge hack UK supermarkets narrowly avoided?
findings.summary_md: Pen Test Partners describes how Neil McCourt of Omega Solutions found a significant flaw in Resource Data Management refrigeration controllers and how its hardware team validated it and found additional issues. The post says RDM's initial customer advisory RDM-SA-2026-001, dated 2 November and revised 3 November, lacked impact detail and independent validation, and that Omega alerted the NCSC before a wider industry notification effort. The researchers used Shodan to locate exposed controllers and contact large operators, say smaller cold-chain operators may still be exposed, and withhold the exploit method while advising removal from the public internet and firmware updates.

findings.title: Swift action to secure UK supermarket controls
findings.summary_md: Cooling Post reports that Glasgow-based Resource Data Management released new firmware after security firms found vulnerabilities in its supermarket controllers, which are more common in the UK than Danfoss units. It says thousands of RDM controllers were exposed, that significant operators were contacted and that smaller cold-chain operators may remain exposed. The trade outlet advises verifying that controllers are not reachable from the public internet and using a VPN or private APN where cellular modems are in use.

findings.title: UK operation wards off risk of cyber-attack on supermarket fridges and freezers
findings.summary_md: The Guardian reports that an operation led by Whitehall and the NCSC followed the discovery of weaknesses in RDM devices by Omega Solutions employee Neil McCourt and validation by Pen Test Partners. Garry Turner-Smith of Omega said an attacker with full control of vulnerable RDM data managers could interfere with refrigeration across multiple sites. Ken Munro said the discovery method was not published, that many thousands of controllers at small stores were still exposed, and that operators should take controllers off the public internet or apply updated firmware.
